Is this issue ready to be implemented or are there any areas that need to be cleared up?

Add a Low-Stock Inventory Monitoring Dashboard #62

User Story
As a store manager, I want to view and filter low-stock inventory items in one place so that I can quickly identify which products require restocking without checking each item individually.

User Scenario
A store manager opens the inventory section of the Medusa admin dashboard and selects a new low-stock monitoring view. The page displays inventory items with quantities at or below their configured thresholds, including items that are completely out of stock. The manager filters the list to show only out-of-stock items at a particular stock location. They then select an item to navigate to its inventory details and update its quantity using existing inventory management functionality.

Acceptance Criteria
A low-stock monitoring view is accessible from the inventory section of the admin dashboard.
The view displays inventory items classified as "Low Stock" or "Out of Stock" using the threshold logic introduced in the prerequisite issue.
Each entry displays the inventory item name, current available quantity, configured threshold, and stock status.
Store managers can filter results by stock status ("Low Stock," "Out of Stock," or both).
Store managers can filter results by stock location.
Selecting an item navigates to its existing inventory detail page.
The view displays an appropriate empty state when no inventory items match the selected filters.
Inventory quantities and stock statuses reflect current inventory data when the page is loaded or refreshed.
Automated tests verify filtering, displayed stock statuses, and empty-state behavior.
Out of Scope
Configuring or editing low-stock thresholds (covered in the prerequisite issue).
Email, SMS, or push notifications.
Automatic inventory replenishment.
Bulk inventory adjustments directly from the monitoring view.
Historical inventory trends or predictive stock forecasting.
Open Questions
Should the monitoring view be a separate admin page or a tab within the existing inventory page?
Should inventory items be sorted by lowest available quantity, or by how far below their thresholds they are?
Should the view display each inventory item separately for each stock location?

```text
Issue #61: configurable low-stock threshold and "Low Stock" / "Out of Stock" labels in the admin inventory list.

Decided by the user (2026-11-08):
- Threshold is per inventory item (column on `InventoryItem`), not per location level. Per-location is a possible follow-up.
- Items without a set threshold use 10 (keeps the hardcoded `< 10` behavior from #18, commit 7fe156c453).
- Stored as a column default: `low_stock_threshold: model.number().default(10)`, not nullable. Migration backfills existing rows to 10. Setting 0 turns the low-stock warning off for that item; "Out of Stock" still shows.
- An item with no location levels (null stocked/reserved sums) is "Out of Stock".

Found in review (2026-11-07); defaults accepted by the user (2026-11-08), no need to ask the issue author:
- #61 replaces the #18 badge in `use-inventory-table-columns.tsx`. That badge uses `stocked_quantity`, `< 10`, shows "Low stock" at 0, has untranslated text, and its spec tests a copy of the logic, not the column. So the "existing functionality unchanged" criterion can't hold literally.
- Item-level available quantity = summed stocked - summed reserved (the item only has those two lazy SUM formulas; `available_quantity` exists only per level). Incoming excluded.
- Open Q3 ("items that don't track stock") is moot: `manage_inventory` is on ProductVariant, not on inventory items.
- List page only, no filter/sort by status; CSV import does not take the field.

Implemented 2026-11-08 on branch feat/issue-61-configurable-low-stock-thresholds, uncommitted (user commits and opens the PR themselves). Notes for the PR:
- API validator also has `.max(2147483647)` (Postgres integer limit) so too-large values give 400, not a DB 500. Null is rejected (column not nullable).
- Dashboard labels use sentence case ("Low stock", "Out of stock") to match existing keys like "In stock"; StatusBadge orange/red; `getStockStatus` exported from use-inventory-table-columns.tsx.
- Edit form rejects empty/whitespace input instead of coercing it to 0. Schema lives in edit-inventory-item/schema.ts (dashboard lint forbids non-component exports from component files) with schema.spec.ts.
- reservations.spec.ts needed `low_stock_threshold: 10` added to two exact-match inventory item objects.
- Tech debt encountered: `yarn migration:create` in the inventory module also emitted unrelated raw_* column ALTERs and snapshot format churn; kept only the new column. payloads.ts already failed Prettier on develop (AdminUpdateInventoryItem line); left as is.

**Why:** Agreed before implementation; list in the PR description per [[pr-description-format]].
**How to apply:** Validator is `z.number().int().min(0).optional()` (no null, since the column is not nullable). Treat null quantity sums as 0 in the status function so no-location items fall into "Out of Stock".
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-09 14:33:37Z)**_

Not quite ready. Three of the gaps affect the design, so get them answered before starting. The rest can go in as stated defaults.

## Need answers first

**1. What does "filter by stock location" mean when the threshold is per item?**
Issue #61 put one threshold on each inventory item. Status is worked out from stocked minus reserved, summed across *all* locations (`getStockStatus` in [use-inventory-table-columns.tsx:12](packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/inventory/inventory-list/components/use-inventory-table-columns.tsx#L12)). The list API already accepts `location_levels.location_id`, but that filter only narrows *which items* come back. It doesn't change the summed quantities. So "out-of-stock items at location X" could mean either:
- **(a)** items stocked at X whose *total* is out of stock. This is cheap, but an item with 0 at X and 500 elsewhere won't show up.
- **(b)** items whose quantity *at X* is out of stock, comparing that location's available quantity to the item's threshold. This matches the scenario, but every status becomes per location.

Open question 3 ("one row per location?") is the same decision. I'd go with (b): one row per item and location, available quantity taken from that location's level, threshold from the item. That's the only reading where "out of stock at location X" is true.

**2. Is server-side filtering in scope?**
`stocked_quantity` and `reserved_quantity` are computed SUM fields ([inventory-item.ts:29-30](packages/modules/inventory/src/models/inventory-item.ts#L29-L30)), and the API has no status filter. Filtering in the browser only works on the current page of 20 items, so pages would come out partly empty and the counts would be wrong. Doing it properly needs a new backend query, probably over inventory levels, which also fits answer (b) above. That's a much bigger issue than a dashboard view, and the issue should say it's included.

**3. Separate page or tab (open question 1)?**
The cheapest option is neither. Add a stock-status filter to the existing inventory list, plus a location filter if it doesn't already have one. That covers "view and filter in one place" with no new route. If the team specifically wants a dedicated page, I'd make it a route at `/inventory/low-stock`, linked from the inventory list. Either way, someone has to choose.

## Fine as defaults (state them in the issue or PR)
- **Sort (open question 2):** by available quantity, lowest first, so out-of-stock items come first. Sorting by distance below threshold puts items with threshold 0 in odd places and is harder to explain.
- **"Available quantity"** is stocked minus reserved, ignoring incoming, the same as #61.
- **Items with no location levels** count as "Out of Stock" (from #61). With option (b) they have no rows, so they disappear when a location filter is applied.
- **Threshold 0** means the item never shows as Low Stock but can still be Out of Stock (from #61).
- **"Inventory item name"** is the item's `title`, which is optional. Fall back to the SKU when it's empty.
- **"Reflects current data"** means data is fetched when the page loads, with no live updates or polling.
- **Tests:** if filtering moves to the server, the filtering criterion needs an HTTP integration test in `integration-tests/http/__tests__/inventory/`, not just Vitest.

I only read the #61 code and the list validators. I didn't check how big a per-level query would be or whether the dashboard's existing filter components support a status filter. Questions 1 and 2 decide whether #62 needs backend work, so its size depends on those answers.

## The smallest complete change

Take the first option that fully works:

1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 23:30:39Z)**_

Showing stock per item fixes the biggest problem. The view uses the same status logic as #61, and the location filter is gone. It's almost ready, but three things are still open.

**1. Where does the status filter run? This one decides the size of the work.**
An item's stocked and reserved totals are calculated when the data is read, and the inventory list API can't filter on them. So if only the dashboard filters, it filters one page of 20 items at a time. Pages come out partly empty and the item counts are wrong. Pick one:
- **(a) Backend filter:** add a `stock_status` filter to the inventory items list endpoint. This is correct at any number of items, but it's real backend work plus HTTP integration tests.
- **(b) Dashboard only:** load all items and filter them in the browser. It's quick, but it gets slow as the catalog grows, and it should be written down as a known limit.

I'd go with (a). The issue never mentions backend work, so whichever you pick, add one line saying it.

**2. Separate page or tab (open question 1)?**
The smallest option is a stock-status filter and a threshold column on the existing inventory list, since it already links each item to its detail page. If the team wants a dedicated view, I'd make it a separate page at `/inventory/low-stock`, linked from the inventory list. Either is fine, but someone has to choose.

**3. Sort order (open question 2)?**
I suggest lowest available quantity first, so out-of-stock items lead. Sorting by how far below threshold an item is ranks items oddly when their threshold is 0.

Once these are answered, either in the issue or as defaults you write into the PR, it's ready to implement. I've saved the per-item decision and these open points to memory for the PR description.

I didn't check whether the Medusa data layer can filter on the calculated totals directly. If it can't, option (a) needs a custom query.

```text
import {
  AuthenticatedMedusaRequest,
  MedusaResponse,
} from "@medusajs/framework/http"
import {
  ContainerRegistrationKeys,
  remoteQueryObjectFromString,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"

import { createInventoryItemsWorkflow } from "@medusajs/core-flows"
import { refetchInventoryItem } from "./helpers"
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/framework/types"

export const POST = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<
    HttpTypes.AdminCreateInventoryItem,
    HttpTypes.SelectParams
  >,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminInventoryItemResponse>
) => {
  const { result } = await createInventoryItemsWorkflow(req.scope).run({
    input: { items: [req.validatedBody] },
  })

  const inventoryItem = await refetchInventoryItem(
    result[0].id,
    req.scope,
    req.queryConfig.fields
  )

  res.status(200).json({ inventory_item: inventoryItem })
}

export const GET = async (
  req: AuthenticatedMedusaRequest<HttpTypes.AdminInventoryItemsParams>,
  res: MedusaResponse<HttpTypes.AdminInventoryItemListResponse>
) => {
  const remoteQuery = req.scope.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.REMOTE_QUERY)

  const query = remoteQueryObjectFromString({
    entryPoint: "inventory_items",
    variables: {
      filters: req.filterableFields,
      ...req.queryConfig.pagination,
    },
    fields: req.queryConfig.fields,
  })

  const { rows: inventory_items, metadata } = await remoteQuery({
    ...query,
  })

  res.status(200).json({
    inventory_items,
    count: metadata.count,
    offset: metadata.skip,
    limit: metadata.take,
  })
}
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
import {
  BigNumber,
  isDefined,
  MathBN,
  toMikroORMEntity,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"
import { Formula, OnInit } from "@medusajs/framework/mikro-orm/core"

import InventoryItem from "../models/inventory-item"
import InventoryLevel from "../models/inventory-level"

function applyHook() {
  const MikroORMEntity = toMikroORMEntity(InventoryLevel)

  MikroORMEntity.prototype["onInit"] = function () {
    if (isDefined(this.stocked_quantity) && isDefined(this.reserved_quantity)) {
      this.available_quantity = new BigNumber(
        MathBN.sub(this.raw_stocked_quantity, this.raw_reserved_quantity)
      )
    }
  }

  OnInit()(MikroORMEntity.prototype, "onInit")
}

function applyFormulas() {
  const MikroORMEntity = toMikroORMEntity(InventoryItem)

  Formula(
    (item) =>
      `(SELECT SUM(reserved_quantity) FROM inventory_level il WHERE il.inventory_item_id = ${item}.id AND il.deleted_at IS NULL)`,
    { lazy: true, serializer: Number, hidden: true, type: "number" }
  )(MikroORMEntity.prototype, "reserved_quantity")

  Formula(
    (item) =>
      `(SELECT SUM(stocked_quantity) FROM inventory_level il WHERE il.inventory_item_id = ${item}.id AND il.deleted_at IS NULL)`,
    { lazy: true, serializer: Number, hidden: true, type: "number" }
  )(MikroORMEntity.prototype, "stocked_quantity")
}

export const applyEntityHooks = () => {
  applyHook()
  applyFormulas()
}
```

```text
import { Filter } from "../../../../components/table/data-table"
import { useStockLocations } from "../../../../hooks/api/stock-locations"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"

export const useInventoryTableFilters = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const { stock_locations } = useStockLocations({
    limit: 1000,
  })

  const filters: Filter[] = []

  if (stock_locations) {
    const stockLocationFilter: Filter = {
      type: "select",
      options: stock_locations.map((s) => ({
        label: s.name,
        value: s.id,
      })),
      key: "location_id",
      searchable: true,
      label: t("fields.location"),
    }

    filters.push(stockLocationFilter)
  }

  filters.push({
    type: "string",
    key: "material",
    label: t("fields.material"),
  })

  filters.push({
    type: "string",
    key: "sku",
    label: t("fields.sku"),
  })

  filters.push({
    type: "string",
    key: "mid_code",
    label: t("fields.midCode"),
  })

  filters.push({
    type: "number",
    key: "height",
    label: t("fields.height"),
  })

  filters.push({
    type: "number",
    key: "width",
    label: t("fields.width"),
  })

  filters.push({
    type: "number",
    key: "length",
    label: t("fields.length"),
  })

  filters.push({
    type: "number",
    key: "weight",
    label: t("fields.weight"),
  })

  filters.push({
    type: "select",
    options: [
      { label: t("fields.true"), value: "true" },
      { label: t("fields.false"), value: "false" },
    ],
    key: "requires_shipping",
    multiple: false,
    label: t("fields.requiresShipping"),
  })

  return filters
}
import { HttpTypes } from "@medusajs/types"

import { useQueryParams } from "../../../../hooks/use-query-params"

export const useInventoryTableQuery = ({
  pageSize = 20,
  prefix,
}: {
  pageSize?: number
  prefix?: string
}) => {
  const raw = useQueryParams(
    [
      "id",
      "location_id",
      "q",
      "order",
      "requires_shipping",
      "offset",
      "sku",
      "origin_country",
      "material",
      "mid_code",
      "hs_code",
      "order",
      "weight",
      "width",
      "length",
      "height",
    ],
    prefix
  )

  const {
    offset,
    weight,
    width,
    length,
    height,
    requires_shipping,
    ...params
  } = raw

  const searchParams: HttpTypes.AdminInventoryItemsParams = {
    limit: pageSize,
    offset: offset ? parseInt(offset) : undefined,
    weight: weight ? JSON.parse(weight) : undefined,
    width: width ? JSON.parse(width) : undefined,
    length: length ? JSON.parse(length) : undefined,
    height: height ? JSON.parse(height) : undefined,
    requires_shipping: requires_shipping
      ? JSON.parse(requires_shipping)
      : undefined,
    q: params.q,
    sku: params.sku,
    order: params.order,
    mid_code: params.mid_code,
    hs_code: params.hs_code,
    material: params.material,
    location_levels: {
      location_id: params.location_id || [],
    },
    id: params.id ? params.id.split(",") : undefined,
  }

  return {
    searchParams,
    raw,
  }
}
```

```text
export const useInventoryTableColumns = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()

  return useMemo(
    () => [
      columnHelper.display({
        id: "select",
        header: ({ table }) => {
          return (
            <Checkbox
              checked={
                table.getIsSomePageRowsSelected()
                  ? "indeterminate"
                  : table.getIsAllPageRowsSelected()
              }
              onCheckedChange={(value) =>
                table.toggleAllPageRowsSelected(!!value)
              }
            />
          )
        },
        cell: ({ row }) => {
          return (
            <Checkbox
              checked={row.getIsSelected()}
              onCheckedChange={(value) => row.toggleSelected(!!value)}
              onClick={(e) => {
                e.stopPropagation()
              }}
            />
          )
        },
      }),
      columnHelper.accessor("title", {
        header: t("fields.title"),
        cell: ({ getValue }) => {
          const title = getValue()

          if (!title) {
            return <PlaceholderCell />
          }

          return (
            <div className="flex size-full items-center overflow-hidden">
              <span className="truncate">{title}</span>
            </div>
          )
        },
      }),
      columnHelper.accessor("sku", {
        header: t("fields.sku"),
        cell: ({ getValue }) => {
          const sku = getValue() as string

          if (!sku) {
            return <PlaceholderCell />
          }

          return (
            <div className="flex size-full items-center overflow-hidden">
              <span className="truncate">{sku}</span>
            </div>
          )
        },
      }),
      columnHelper.accessor("reserved_quantity", {
        header: t("inventory.reserved"),
        cell: ({ getValue }) => {
          const quantity = getValue()

          if (Number.isNaN(quantity)) {
            return <PlaceholderCell />
          }

          return (
            <div className="flex size-full items-center overflow-hidden">
              <span className="truncate">{quantity}</span>
            </div>
          )
        },
      }),
      columnHelper.accessor("stocked_quantity", {
        header: t("fields.inStock"),
        cell: ({ getValue, row }) => {
          const quantity = getValue()

          if (Number.isNaN(quantity)) {
            return <PlaceholderCell />
          }

          const status = getStockStatus(row.original)

          return (
            <div className="flex size-full items-center gap-x-2 overflow-hidden">
              <span className="truncate">{quantity}</span>
              {status === "out_of_stock" && (
                <StatusBadge color="red">
                  {t("inventory.outOfStock")}
                </StatusBadge>
              )}
              {status === "low_stock" && (
                <StatusBadge color="orange">
                  {t("inventory.lowStock")}
                </StatusBadge>
              )}
            </div>
          )
        },
      }),
      columnHelper.display({
        id: "actions",
        cell: ({ row }) => <InventoryActions item={row.original} />,
      }),
    ],
    [t]
  )
}
import { Button, Container, Heading, Text } from "@medusajs/ui"

import { RowSelectionState } from "@tanstack/react-table"
import { useState } from "react"
import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next"
import { Link, useNavigate } from "react-router-dom"
import { _DataTable } from "../../../../components/table/data-table"
import { useInventoryItems } from "../../../../hooks/api/inventory"
import { useDataTable } from "../../../../hooks/use-data-table"
import { INVENTORY_ITEM_IDS_KEY } from "../../common/constants"
import { useInventoryTableColumns } from "./use-inventory-table-columns"
import { useInventoryTableFilters } from "./use-inventory-table-filters"
import { useInventoryTableQuery } from "./use-inventory-table-query"

const PAGE_SIZE = 20

export const InventoryListTable = () => {
  const { t } = useTranslation()
  const navigate = useNavigate()

  const [selection, setSelection] = useState<RowSelectionState>({})

  const { searchParams, raw } = useInventoryTableQuery({
    pageSize: PAGE_SIZE,
  })

  const {
    inventory_items,
    count,
    isPending: isLoading,
    isError,
    error,
  } = useInventoryItems({
    ...searchParams,
  })

  const filters = useInventoryTableFilters()
  const columns = useInventoryTableColumns()

  const { table } = useDataTable({
    data: inventory_items,
    columns,
    count,
    enablePagination: true,
    getRowId: (row) => row.id,
    pageSize: PAGE_SIZE,
    enableRowSelection: true,
    rowSelection: {
      state: selection,
      updater: setSelection,
    },
  })

  if (isError) {
    throw error
  }

  return (
    <Container className="divide-y p-0">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between px-6 py-4">
        <div>
          <Heading>{t("inventory.domain")}</Heading>
          <Text className="text-ui-fg-subtle" size="small">
            {t("inventory.subtitle")}
          </Text>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-x-2">
          <Button size="small" variant="secondary" asChild>
            <Link to="import">{t("actions.import")}</Link>
          </Button>
          <Button size="small" variant="secondary" asChild>
            <Link to="create">{t("actions.create")}</Link>
          </Button>
        </div>
      </div>
      <_DataTable
        table={table}
        columns={columns}
        pageSize={PAGE_SIZE}
        count={count}
        isLoading={isLoading}
        pagination
        search
        filters={filters}
        queryObject={raw}
        orderBy={[
          { key: "title", label: t("fields.title") },
          { key: "sku", label: t("fields.sku") },
          { key: "stocked_quantity", label: t("fields.inStock") },
          { key: "reserved_quantity", label: t("inventory.reserved") },
        ]}
        navigateTo={(row) => `${row.id}`}
        commands={[
          {
            action: async (selection) => {
              navigate(
                `stock?${INVENTORY_ITEM_IDS_KEY}=${Object.keys(selection).join(
                  ","
                )}`
              )
            },
            label: t("inventory.stock.action"),
            shortcut: "i",
          },
        ]}
      />
    </Container>
  )
}
```

```text
---
name: pr-description-format
description: The exact section structure the user wants for every PR description in this repo
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 1bc7bf15-343c-4498-9d39-89fc17070812
  modified: 2026-11-08T16:55:03.137Z
---

PR descriptions must follow the repo template with the user's extended structure (given 2026-10-07):

- `## Summary` with **What**, **Why**, **How**, **Testing** — each followed by the template's prompt line in italics-free form (e.g. "**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?") and then the answer. What = short paragraph + bullets; Why = "Closes #N" + one or two sentences; How = workflows/steps changed + "A changeset is included (patch)."; Testing = what the spec covers (bullets), "Results from a local run:" bullets, and a bash block to reproduce.
- `---` then `## Examples` with a short ts snippet.
- `---` then `## Design`: **Decision**, **Alternatives considered** (bullets), **Rationale**, **Consequences**, **Other decisions** (bold-lead bullets).
- `---` then `## Tech Debt` (added 2026-10-25): **Introduced:** shortcuts/compromises made and why; **Encountered:** pre-existing debt hit and how it was handled. Write "None." if none.
- `---` then `## Test Evidence` (Sprint 3, added 2026-11-08): table `| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |`, one row per AC (bug: Expected Behavior; no product change: "N/A" + why). Test(s) = test name/file, or "Manual: steps → what you saw". Level = unit/integration/E2E/manual. Source = AC, issue discussion, docs, upstream behavior, or other (explained) — never the code's own output. Then **Not tested automatically, and why:** and **AI-written tests:** (which tests AI wrote and how expected values were checked). With no CI, list the commands run and results. This replaces the How-it-was-tested content: Summary's **Testing** just points to it plus repro steps.
- Design decisions must each name at least two concrete alternatives (course grading requirement).
- `---` then `## Checklist` with four items (changeset, tests, verified locally, linked issue).
- `---` then `## Additional Context` with **CI** and **Limitations** bullets.

Keep each part brief. Put the design decisions from the issue's memory note (e.g. [[subscriptions-design-decisions]], [[issue-38-design-decisions]]) under Design.

**Why:** The user's team reviews PRs against this format; earlier descriptions that skipped sections had to be redone.
**How to apply:** Use this structure for any PR description in this repo, even a small chore PR.
```
</details></tool-use>

```markdown
---
name: issue-62-design-decisions
description: Agreed scope and choices for issue #62 low-stock monitoring (server-side stock_status filter on existing inventory list); go in PR design-decisions
metadata:
  type: project
---

Issue #62: low-stock monitoring in admin inventory section. Builds on [[issue-61-design-decisions]].

Decided (2026-11-16):
- Per item, not per location (teammate). Status = summed stocked - reserved across locations vs item threshold, same as #61 `getStockStatus`. Location removed from issue; per-location is future work.
- Server-side filter (user picked over client-side filtering, which breaks pagination). New `stock_status` query param on GET /admin/inventory-items (`low_stock` | `out_of_stock` | array). "Stick to exactly what the issue says": no extras.
- No new page: stock-status filter + threshold column on the existing inventory list (user ok'd). Alternatives: separate /inventory/low-stock route, tab.
- Sort by lowest available quantity when stock_status is set (user). Alternative: distance below threshold (odd with threshold 0). Request `order` is ignored while the filter is set.

Implementation notes (for PR):
- Inventory module overrides listInventoryItems / listAndCountInventoryItems; a knex GROUP BY/HAVING query gets ids sorted by available asc, then intersects with other filters and paginates in memory. Tech debt (introduced): loads all matching ids per request; `shortcut:` comment in inventory-module.ts.
- stock_status kept out of $and/$or in the validator (service only handles top level).
- Added an Available column because AC3 requires available quantity; existing list only showed reserved and in stock.

**Why:** Goes in PR description per [[pr-description-format]].
**How to apply:** Use these as the Design section; record further decisions here as they come.

```

```text
// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { cleanup, render, renderHook, screen } from "@testing-library/react"
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"

vi.hoisted(() => {
  const g = global as any
  g.__BACKEND_URL__ = "http://localhost:9000"
  g.__AUTH_TYPE__ = "session"
  g.__JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY__ = ""
})

vi.mock("react-i18next", () => ({
  useTranslation: () => ({
    t: (key: string) => key,
  }),
}))

vi.mock("./inventory-actions", () => ({
  InventoryActions: () => <div />,
}))

import {
  getStockStatus,
  useInventoryTableColumns,
} from "./use-inventory-table-columns"

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup()
})

const item = (
  stocked_quantity: number | null,
  reserved_quantity: number | null,
  low_stock_threshold = 10
) => ({ stocked_quantity, reserved_quantity, low_stock_threshold } as any)

describe("getStockStatus", () => {
  it("is out of stock when available quantity is 0", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(5, 5))).toBe("out_of_stock")
  })

  it("is out of stock when available quantity is negative", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(2, 3))).toBe("out_of_stock")
  })

  it("is out of stock when the item has no location levels", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(null, null))).toBe("out_of_stock")
  })

  it("is out of stock at 0 even when the threshold is 0", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(0, 0, 0))).toBe("out_of_stock")
  })

  it("is low stock when available quantity equals the threshold", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(12, 2, 10))).toBe("low_stock")
  })

  it("is low stock at 1 available", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(1, 0, 10))).toBe("low_stock")
  })

  it("has no status when available quantity is above the threshold", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(13, 2, 10))).toBeNull()
  })

  it("uses available, not stocked, quantity", () => {
    // 20 stocked is above 10, but 20 - 15 reserved = 5 is not
    expect(getStockStatus(item(20, 15, 10))).toBe("low_stock")
  })

  it("never shows low stock when the threshold is 0", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(1, 0, 0))).toBeNull()
  })

  it("respects a custom threshold", () => {
    expect(getStockStatus(item(50, 0, 50))).toBe("low_stock")
    expect(getStockStatus(item(51, 0, 50))).toBeNull()
  })
})
```

```typescript
// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { cleanup, render, screen } from "@testing-library/react"
import { MemoryRouter } from "react-router-dom"
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest"

// The API hooks pull in the SDK client, which reads these globals at load.
vi.hoisted(() => {
  const g = global as any
  g.__BACKEND_URL__ = "http://localhost:9000"
  g.__AUTH_TYPE__ = "session"
  g.__JWT_TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY__ = ""
})

const { useInventoryItems } = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  useInventoryItems: vi.fn(),
}))

vi.mock("../../../../hooks/api/inventory", () => ({ useInventoryItems }))

vi.mock("../../../../hooks/api/stock-locations", () => ({
  useStockLocations: () => ({ stock_locations: [] }),
}))

vi.mock("react-i18next", () => ({
  useTranslation: () => ({ t: (key: string) => key }),
}))

vi.mock("./inventory-actions", () => ({
  InventoryActions: () => null,
}))

import { InventoryListTable } from "./inventory-list-table"
import { useInventoryTableFilters } from "./use-inventory-table-filters"
import { renderHook } from "@testing-library/react"

const renderAt = (url: string) =>
  render(
    <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[url]}>
      <InventoryListTable />
    </MemoryRouter>
  )

const respondWith = (inventory_items: any[]) =>
  useInventoryItems.mockReturnValue({
    inventory_items,
    count: inventory_items.length,
    isPending: false,
    isError: false,
  })

afterEach(() => {
  cleanup()
  useInventoryItems.mockReset()
})

describe("inventory list stock status filter", () => {
  it("offers low stock and out of stock as filter options", () => {
    const { result } = renderHook(() => useInventoryTableFilters())
    const filter = result.current.find((f) => f.key === "stock_status") as any

    expect(filter.options.map((o: any) => o.value)).toEqual([
      "low_stock",
      "out_of_stock",
    ])
  })

  it.each([
    ["out_of_stock", ["out_of_stock"]],
    ["low_stock%2Cout_of_stock", ["low_stock", "out_of_stock"]],
  ])(
    "sends stock_status=%s to the API as a list",
    (param, expected) => {
      respondWith([])
      renderAt(`/?stock_status=${param}`)

      expect(useInventoryItems).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        expect.objectContaining({ stock_status: expected })
      )
    }
  )

  it("does not send stock_status when the filter is not set", () => {
    respondWith([])
    renderAt("/")

    expect(useInventoryItems.mock.calls[0][0].stock_status).toBeUndefined()
  })

  it("shows the no results state when no items match the filter", () => {
    respondWith([])
    renderAt("/?stock_status=out_of_stock")

    expect(screen.getByText("general.noResultsTitle")).toBeTruthy()
  })

  it("shows available quantity, threshold and status for each item", () => {
    respondWith([
      {
        id: "iitem_1",
        title: "Shirt",
        sku: "shirt",
        stocked_quantity: 12,
        reserved_quantity: 5,
        low_stock_threshold: 10,
      },
    ])
    renderAt("/?stock_status=low_stock")

    const row = screen.getByText("Shirt").closest("tr")!
    const cells = Array.from(row.querySelectorAll("td")).map(
      (td) => td.textContent
    )

    // title, sku, reserved, in stock + badge, available, threshold
    expect(cells).toEqual(
      expect.arrayContaining([
        "Shirt",
        "5",
        "12inventory.lowStock",
        "7",
        "10",
      ])
    )
  })
})
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-16 23:42:02Z)**_

Issue #62 is implemented on this branch and the tests pass. Nothing is committed yet.

**API:** `GET /admin/inventory-items` takes a new `stock_status` filter (`low_stock`, `out_of_stock`, or both). It uses the same rule as #61: available quantity = stocked − reserved, summed across all locations, compared against the item's threshold. Results come back lowest available quantity first.
- The filtering happens in the database, so pagination and item counts are correct.
- It works alongside the existing filters, like SKU and search.
- An unknown status value returns a 400 error.
- While the filter is set, any other sort order from the request is ignored.

**Dashboard:** the existing inventory list now has a stock status filter, an Available column and a Low stock threshold column. When nothing matches the filter, the table's existing "No results" state shows. Clicking a row still opens the item's detail page.

I added the Available column because the issue says each entry shows the current available quantity, and the list only showed reserved and in-stock counts. The main logic is in [inventory-module.ts](packages/modules/inventory/src/services/inventory-module.ts).

**Tests:**
- **API:** 8 new tests in [inventory.spec.ts](integration-tests/http/__tests__/inventory/admin/inventory.spec.ts) cover each status, including one item that is low only because of a reservation and one with no stock locations. They also cover sort order, paging, combining with another filter, the empty result, an unchanged list without the filter, and the 400. All pass.
- **Dashboard:** a new spec, [inventory-list-stock-status.spec.tsx](packages/admin/dashboard/src/routes/inventory/inventory-list/components/inventory-list-stock-status.spec.tsx), checks the filter options, the value sent to the API, the empty state, and the columns shown. All 21 inventory list tests pass.
- **Regressions:** the full inventory and reservation API suites (71 tests) and the inventory module suite (35) pass. The dashboard typecheck reports the same 6 errors with and without my changes, all in core types files.

**Housekeeping:** I added a changeset. Running the module tests generated a `.snapshot-medusa-inventory-integration-1.json` file, which I deleted. All of the design decisions are saved for the PR's Design section.

**Known limit:** each filtered request loads the ID of every matching item to keep the sort correct across pages. It's fine at normal catalog sizes, and it's marked with a `shortcut:` comment in the code. I didn't click through the dashboard in a running app; it's only covered by tests.

Send the mutation testing details whenever you're ready and I'll add them to the saved PR format.

D6 - Mutation Testing (new)¶
This is a new individual deliverable.

What it is. A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code (mutants), such as flipping a condition or changing a boundary value, and runs your tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is killed. If all tests pass, the mutant survived: your tests did not notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.

What to do. For one of your issues whose PR changes source code and tests (CSCI 535: two such issues; your small issue may be one of them):

Run a mutation testing tool on the source files changed by your PR(s) for that issue. Do not run it on the whole project.
Using the tool's report, analyze every surviving mutant: is it equivalent (it behaves exactly like the original code, so no test can kill it), or does it reveal a gap in your tests? If there are more than 10 surviving mutants, analyze at least 10, starting with those in lines your PR added or changed.
Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a surviving mutant that revealed a gap. Re-run the tool to confirm it is killed. If no surviving mutant reveals a gap (all are killed or equivalent), say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table; that completes this step.
Answer the questions in the template below.
Evidence. Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report (StrykerJS: add "json" to reporters; Gremlins: --output=<file>.json; go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text file). Commit the report from your first run and from your re-run as docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json and -after.json (.txt for go-mutesting). The mutation scores you list must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.

A tool is required. Manual mutation does not count.

Stack	Tool
TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest (Actual Budget, Cal.diy, Excalidraw, Outline, Gitea frontend)	StrykerJS with the Vitest runner
TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa)	StrykerJS with the Jest runner
Go (Gitea backend)	Gremlins or go-mutesting
Set it up early. Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is real work: builds, services, and choosing which tests run. Each student configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits the configuration they used. You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are encouraged to), as long as you run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

Common problems to watch for:

The tool stops before mutating. Tools first run your tests on the unchanged code. If any of the selected tests fail, the run stops. Fix or exclude failing tests first (this is where your baseline run helps).
Tests run against built code. If your tests run against compiled output (for example, a dist folder) instead of the source, mutants in the source are never seen by the tests. Configure the tool to rebuild before testing, or choose tests that run on source.
Tests need services. Some test suites need a database or another service running. Start them before running the tool.
False survivors. If you limit which tests run (for example, with Vitest's dir option), make sure the tests that cover the mutated files are included. Otherwise, mutants that some test would catch are reported as survived or not covered. Before writing a new test for a survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
Long runs. Mutating only the files changed by your PR keeps run time manageable.
If you are blocked

If you cannot get the tool to run, first ask your teammates: someone may already have a working setup. If you are still stuck, tell the TA as early as possible, with the errors you got and the AI log of what you tried. The TA will help you debug it. If it still cannot be made to work, the TA may approve running the tool on a different issue or a different part of your code instead. Problems reported at the end of the sprint will not excuse a missing D6.

Submission: docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md, using this template:
</pasted_content id="389e">

```bash
block='''
      describe("stock_status filter", () => {
        let reservedItem: InventoryItemDTO
        let noLevelsItem: InventoryItemDTO
        let lowItem: InventoryItemDTO
        let zeroItem: InventoryItemDTO

        const createWithStock = async (
          sku: string,
          stocked: number,
          extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}
        ) => {
          const item = await service.createInventoryItems({ sku, ...extra })
          await service.createInventoryLevels({
            inventory_item_id: item.id,
            location_id: "location-1",
            stocked_quantity: stocked,
          })
          return item
        }

        // Available = stocked - reserved, summed over locations.
        // Out of stock: available <= 0. Low stock: 0 < available <= threshold.
        beforeEach(async () => {
          // 7 + 5 stocked - 5 reserved = 7: low only because of the reservation
          reservedItem = await createWithStock("reserved", 7)
          await service.createInventoryLevels({
            inventory_item_id: reservedItem.id,
            location_id: "location-2",
            stocked_quantity: 5,
          })
          await service.createReservationItems({
            inventory_item_id: reservedItem.id,
            location_id: "location-2",
            quantity: 5,
          })
          noLevelsItem = await service.createInventoryItems({ sku: "none" })
          lowItem = await createWithStock("low", 3)
          zeroItem = await createWithStock("zero", 0)
          await createWithStock("healthy", 50)
          await createWithStock("threshold-off", 2, { low_stock_threshold: 0 })
        })

        const ids = (items: InventoryItemDTO[]) => items.map((i) => i.id)

        it("lists low stock items, lowest available quantity first", async () => {
          const [items, count] = await service.listAndCountInventoryItems({
            stock_status: "low_stock",
          })

          expect(count).toEqual(2)
          expect(ids(items)).toEqual([lowItem.id, reservedItem.id])
        })

        it("lists out of stock items, including items without levels", async () => {
          const [items, count] = await service.listAndCountInventoryItems({
            stock_status: ["out_of_stock"],
          })

          expect(count).toEqual(2)
          expect(ids(items).sort()).toEqual([noLevelsItem.id, zeroItem.id].sort())
        })

        it("lists both statuses with out of stock items first", async () => {
          const [items, count] = await service.listAndCountInventoryItems({
            stock_status: ["low_stock", "out_of_stock"],
          })

          expect(count).toEqual(4)
          expect(ids(items).slice(0, 2).sort()).toEqual(
            [noLevelsItem.id, zeroItem.id].sort()
          )
          expect(ids(items).slice(2)).toEqual([lowItem.id, reservedItem.id])
        })

        it("paginates in quantity order and counts all matches", async () => {
          const [items, count] = await service.listAndCountInventoryItems(
            { stock_status: "low_stock" },
            { skip: 1, take: 1 }
          )

          expect(count).toEqual(2)
          expect(ids(items)).toEqual([reservedItem.id])
        })

        it("combines with other filters", async () => {
          const [items, count] = await service.listAndCountInventoryItems({
            stock_status: "low_stock",
            sku: "reserved",
          })

          expect(count).toEqual(1)
          expect(ids(items)).toEqual([reservedItem.id])
        })

        it("returns nothing when no items match", async () => {
          const [items, count] = await service.listAndCountInventoryItems({
            stock_status: "low_stock",
            sku: "missing",
          })

          expect(items).toEqual([])
          expect(count).toEqual(0)
        })

        it("applies the filter in listInventoryItems too", async () => {
          const items = await service.listInventoryItems({
            stock_status: "low_stock",
          })

          expect(ids(items)).toEqual([lowItem.id, reservedItem.id])
        })

        it("does not change results when the filter is not set", async () => {
          const [, count] = await service.listAndCountInventoryItems({})

          expect(count).toEqual(6)
        })

        it("rejects an unknown stock status", async () => {
          const error = await service
            .listAndCountInventoryItems({ stock_status: "in_stock" as any })
            .catch((e) => e)

          expect(error.message).toEqual("Invalid stock status: in_stock")
        })
      })
'''
```

```cjs
// on parameters that have a default value, so every `@MedusaContext() context:
// Context = {}` loses its decorator and @EmitEvents fails at runtime. This puts
// them back before building dist/, which the module tests load.
const fs = require("fs")
const { execSync } = require("child_process")

const file = "src/services/inventory-module.ts"
const pattern = /(?<!@MedusaContext\(\) )\bcontext: Context = \{\}/g

const source = fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8")
const restored = (source.match(pattern) ?? []).length
fs.writeFileSync(
  file,
  source.replace(pattern, "@MedusaContext() context: Context = {}")
)
console.log(`stryker-build: restored ${restored} @MedusaContext() decorators`)

execSync("yarn build", { stdio: "inherit" })

```

```markdown
# Mutation testing: Issue #62 -- Add a Low-Stock Inventory Monitoring Dashboard

**PR(s):** #TODO  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Jest runner (`@stryker-mutator/core`, `@stryker-mutator/jest-runner`)  **Config:** [stryker.config.json](../../../packages/modules/inventory/stryker.config.json) and its build step [stryker-build.cjs](../../../packages/modules/inventory/stryker-build.cjs) (my own setup; no teammate setup existed)  **Command:** `cd packages/modules/inventory && npx stryker run` (Postgres running)

**Setup problems solved:**
- The module tests load `dist/`, not `src/`. The config therefore rebuilds the package after Stryker instruments the file (`buildCommand`), and runs `inPlace` because the sandbox copy breaks the package tsconfig's relative `extends`.
- Babel, which Stryker uses to instrument the file, drops parameter decorators on parameters with a default value. Every `@MedusaContext() context: Context = {}` lost its decorator, so 8 existing tests failed in the initial run. This happens in both Babel 8 (Stryker 10) and Babel 7.29 (Stryker 9). `stryker-build.cjs` restores the 35 decorators before building.
- `moduleIntegrationTestRunner` wraps suites in `describe("")`, so Stryker's per-test coverage IDs never match Jest's test names, and every mutant was reported as uncovered. `coverageAnalysis` is set to `all`, so every test runs against every mutant.
- `concurrency` is 1 because every test run uses the same test database name.
```

````markdown
## Summary

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

Store managers can now list only low-stock or out-of-stock inventory items from the existing admin inventory list. Results are sorted by lowest available quantity first.

- `GET /admin/inventory-items` accepts `stock_status` (`low_stock`, `out_of_stock`, or both). Filtering, sorting, paging and counts happen in the database query.
- The admin inventory list has a "Stock status" filter and new **Available** and **Low stock threshold** columns.
- Mutation testing (D6) setup and reports for this issue are included.

**Why** — Why are these changes being made?

Closes #62. Managers had to scan every item to find what needs restocking. This uses the per-item threshold from #61 to show only items that are low or out of stock.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

- **Inventory module:** `listInventoryItems` / `listAndCountInventoryItems` handle a `stock_status` filter. A `GROUP BY` / `HAVING` query finds matching item ids, sorted by available quantity (stocked minus reserved, summed over locations, lowest first). The ids are intersected with the other filters, the requested page is taken, and the page is loaded with the caller's fields and relations. Without `stock_status`, the methods behave exactly as before.
- **API:** `stock_status` added to the list validator (outside `$and` / `$or`) and to `AdminInventoryItemsParams` / `FilterableInventoryItemProps`.
- **Dashboard:** status filter, query param, Available and threshold columns, and a "Stock status" translation key. The empty filtered list uses the table's existing "No results" state.
- **Dev tooling:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 and its Jest runner added as root dev dependencies; Stryker output added to `.gitignore`.

A changeset is included (patch).

**Testing** — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

See **Test Evidence** below. To reproduce (Postgres running):

```bash
yarn workspace @medusajs/types build && yarn workspace @medusajs/inventory build && yarn workspace @medusajs/medusa build
cd packages/modules/inventory && npx jest integration-tests
cd integration-tests/http && npx jest __tests__/inventory/admin/inventory.spec.ts __tests__/reservations
cd packages/admin/dashboard && npx vitest run src/routes/inventory
cd packages/modules/inventory && npx stryker run   # mutation testing
```

Manual: open Inventory in the admin, add the "Stock status" filter, choose "Out of stock", then open an item.

---

## Examples

```ts
// Out-of-stock items first, then low stock, each group lowest available first
const { inventory_items, count } = await sdk.admin.inventoryItem.list({
  stock_status: ["low_stock", "out_of_stock"],
  limit: 20,
})
```

`GET /admin/inventory-items?stock_status[]=low_stock&stock_status[]=out_of_stock`

---

## Design

**Decision:** Filter by stock status on the server through the existing inventory list endpoint, and expose it as a filter on the existing admin inventory list.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Filter in the dashboard only. Rejected: `stocked_quantity` / `reserved_quantity` are computed SUM fields, so filtering one page of 20 in the browser gives part-empty pages and wrong counts.
- A separate `/inventory/low-stock` page or a tab. Rejected: it needs a new route and table but does nothing the filtered list doesn't. Open question 1, agreed in the issue discussion.
- One row per item and location. Rejected by the team to keep scope; the threshold is per item (#61). Possible follow-up.

**Rationale:** One query parameter on an existing endpoint gives correct paging and counts with no new route. The dashboard change is a filter and two columns on a table managers already use.

**Consequences:**
- While `stock_status` is set, results are always sorted by available quantity, and any `order` in the request is ignored.
- Each filtered request loads the id of every item with the status (see Tech Debt).

**Other decisions:**
- **Status is per item:** available quantity = stocked minus reserved, summed over all locations, compared with the item's `low_stock_threshold`. This is the same rule as `getStockStatus` from #61. Items with no location levels are out of stock. A threshold of 0 never shows low stock.
- **Sort by lowest available quantity** (open question 2). The alternative, distance below threshold, ranks items oddly when the threshold is 0. Ties are broken by id.
- **Available column added:** acceptance criterion 3 requires the available quantity, and the list only showed reserved and in-stock counts. The alternative was relying on the existing columns and expecting managers to subtract.
- **`stock_status` not allowed inside `$and` / `$or`:** the service handles it only at the top level. The alternative was supporting nested status filters, which nobody needs.
- **Location filter:** the existing location filter still works alongside `stock_status`, but status is always computed over all locations.

---

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- The filter loads every matching item id per request to keep the quantity order across pages. This is fine for normal catalogs; it is marked with a `shortcut:` comment in `inventory-module.ts` with when to move the sort fully into SQL.
- `packages/modules/inventory/stryker-build.cjs` works around a Babel bug in the mutation testing setup: Stryker's instrumenter drops `@MedusaContext()` parameter decorators. The workaround is only used by `stryker run`.

**Encountered:**
- `moduleIntegrationTestRunner` wraps suites in `describe("")`, which breaks Stryker's per-test coverage, so the config uses `coverageAnalysis: "all"`.
- Module and HTTP tests run against `dist/`, so packages must be rebuilt before testing source changes.
- The dashboard typecheck has 6 errors in `packages/core/types` with or without this PR; left as is.

---

## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Low-stock view accessible from the inventory section | `inventory-list-stock-status.spec.tsx` › offers low stock and out of stock as filter options; Manual: Inventory → add filter → Stock status → TODO | unit, manual | AC1; issue discussion (filter on the existing list) |
| 2. Items classified as Low Stock / Out of Stock with #61's threshold logic | `inventory.spec.ts` (HTTP) › should list low stock items, lowest available quantity first; should list out of stock items, including items without levels. `inventory-module-service.spec.ts` › stock_status filter › lists low stock… / lists out of stock… | integration | AC2; #61 threshold rule (available = stocked − reserved; out ≤ 0; low ≤ threshold) |
| 3. Each entry shows name, available quantity, threshold, status | `inventory-list-stock-status.spec.tsx` › shows available quantity, threshold and status for each item | unit | AC3 |
| 4. Filter by Low Stock, Out of Stock, or both | HTTP › should list both statuses with out of stock items first; should combine with other filters; should reject an unknown stock status. Dashboard › sends stock_status=… to the API as a list; does not send stock_status when the filter is not set | integration, unit | AC4; sort order from issue discussion (open question 2) |
| 5. Selecting an item opens its inventory detail page | Manual: click a row in the filtered list → TODO | manual | AC5 (existing row navigation, unchanged) |
| 6. Empty state when nothing matches | HTTP › should return an empty list when nothing matches. Module › returns nothing when no item has the status. Dashboard › shows the no results state when no items match the filter | integration, unit | AC6 |
| 7. Quantities and statuses reflect current data on load/refresh | HTTP › should combine with other filters (a reservation made before listing is reflected in the status); Manual: change a quantity, reload the filtered list → TODO | integration, manual | AC7 |
| 8. Automated tests for filtering, statuses, empty state | All of the above, plus paging: HTTP › should paginate in quantity order and count all matches; Module › limits the first page to take | — | AC8 |

**Mutation testing (D6, selected issue):** [docs/sprint3/mutation/62-njpiombino.md](docs/sprint3/mutation/62-njpiombino.md). StrykerJS with the Jest runner on the lines this PR added to `inventory-module.ts`: 77.78% → 84.72%. Tests added to kill survivors:

The 11 remaining survivors are equivalent; each one is explained in the doc.

- The dashboard files and `validators.ts` were not mutation tested. The dashboard uses Vitest, not Jest, and the validator is only exercised by the HTTP suite, which runs against built packages.

## Additional Context
````

````text
## Summary

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

Store managers can now list only low-stock or out-of-stock inventory items from the existing admin inventory list. Results are sorted by lowest available quantity first.

- `GET /admin/inventory-items` accepts `stock_status` (`low_stock`, `out_of_stock`, or both). Filtering, sorting, paging and counts happen in the database query.
- The admin inventory list has a "Stock status" filter and new **Available** and **Low stock threshold** columns.
- Mutation testing (D6) setup and reports for this issue are included.

**Why** — Why are these changes being made?

Closes #62. Managers had to scan every item to find what needs restocking. This uses the per-item threshold from #61 to show only items that are low or out of stock.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

- **Inventory module:** `listInventoryItems` / `listAndCountInventoryItems` handle a `stock_status` filter. A `GROUP BY` / `HAVING` query finds matching item ids, sorted by available quantity (stocked minus reserved, summed over locations, lowest first). The ids are intersected with the other filters, the requested page is taken, and the page is loaded with the caller's fields and relations. Without `stock_status`, the methods behave exactly as before.
- **API:** `stock_status` added to the list validator (outside `$and` / `$or`) and to `AdminInventoryItemsParams` / `FilterableInventoryItemProps`.
- **Dashboard:** status filter, query param, Available and threshold columns, and a "Stock status" translation key. The empty filtered list uses the table's existing "No results" state.
- **Dev tooling:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 and its Jest runner added as root dev dependencies; Stryker output added to `.gitignore`.

A changeset is included (patch).

**Testing** — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

See **Test Evidence** below. To reproduce (Postgres running):

```bash
yarn workspace @medusajs/types build && yarn workspace @medusajs/inventory build && yarn workspace @medusajs/medusa build
cd packages/modules/inventory && npx jest integration-tests
cd integration-tests/http && npx jest __tests__/inventory/admin/inventory.spec.ts __tests__/reservations
cd packages/admin/dashboard && npx vitest run src/routes/inventory
cd packages/modules/inventory && npx stryker run   # mutation testing
```

Manual (`my-store`, after rebuilding `@medusajs/dashboard`): open Inventory in the admin, add the "Stock status" filter, choose "Out of stock", then open an item. Lower an item's stock to see it move into the filtered list.

---

## Examples

```ts
// Out-of-stock items first, then low stock, each group lowest available first
const { inventory_items, count } = await sdk.admin.inventoryItem.list({
  stock_status: ["low_stock", "out_of_stock"],
  limit: 20,
})
```

`GET /admin/inventory-items?stock_status[]=low_stock&stock_status[]=out_of_stock`

---

## Design

**Decision:** Filter by stock status on the server through the existing inventory list endpoint, and expose it as a filter on the existing admin inventory list.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Filter in the dashboard only. Rejected: `stocked_quantity` / `reserved_quantity` are computed SUM fields, so filtering one page of 20 in the browser gives part-empty pages and wrong counts.
- A separate `/inventory/low-stock` page or a tab. Rejected: it needs a new route and table but does nothing the filtered list doesn't. Open question 1, agreed in the issue discussion.
- One row per item and location. Rejected by the team to keep scope; the threshold is per item (#61). Possible follow-up.

**Rationale:** One query parameter on an existing endpoint gives correct paging and counts with no new route. The dashboard change is a filter and two columns on a table managers already use.

**Consequences:**
- While `stock_status` is set, results are always sorted by available quantity, and any `order` in the request is ignored.
- Each filtered request loads the id of every item with the status (see Tech Debt).

**Other decisions:**
- **Status is per item:** available quantity = stocked minus reserved, summed over all locations, compared with the item's `low_stock_threshold`. This is the same rule as `getStockStatus` from #61. Items with no location levels are out of stock. A threshold of 0 never shows low stock.
- **Sort by lowest available quantity** (open question 2). The alternative, distance below threshold, ranks items oddly when the threshold is 0. Ties are broken by id.
- **Available column added:** acceptance criterion 3 requires the available quantity, and the list only showed reserved and in-stock counts. The alternative was relying on the existing columns and expecting managers to subtract.
- **`stock_status` not allowed inside `$and` / `$or`:** the service handles it only at the top level. The alternative was supporting nested status filters, which nobody needs.
- **Location filter:** the existing location filter still works alongside `stock_status`, but status is always computed over all locations.

---

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- The filter loads every matching item id per request to keep the quantity order across pages. This is fine for normal catalogs; it is marked with a `shortcut:` comment in `inventory-module.ts` with when to move the sort fully into SQL.
- `packages/modules/inventory/stryker-build.cjs` works around a Babel bug in the mutation testing setup: Stryker's instrumenter drops `@MedusaContext()` parameter decorators. The workaround is only used by `stryker run`.

**Encountered:**
- `moduleIntegrationTestRunner` wraps suites in `describe("")`, which breaks Stryker's per-test coverage, so the config uses `coverageAnalysis: "all"`.
- Module and HTTP tests run against `dist/`, so packages must be rebuilt before testing source changes.
- The dashboard typecheck has 6 errors in `packages/core/types` with or without this PR; left as is.

---

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Low-stock view accessible from the inventory section | `inventory-list-stock-status.spec.tsx` › offers low stock and out of stock as filter options; Manual: Inventory → Add filter → Stock status → the filter is listed and narrows the list to low/out-of-stock items | unit, manual | AC1; issue discussion (filter on the existing list) |
| 2. Items classified as Low Stock / Out of Stock with #61's threshold logic | `inventory.spec.ts` (HTTP) › should list low stock items, lowest available quantity first; should list out of stock items, including items without levels. `inventory-module-service.spec.ts` › stock_status filter › lists low stock… / lists out of stock… | integration | AC2; #61 threshold rule (available = stocked − reserved; out ≤ 0; low ≤ threshold) |
| 3. Each entry shows name, available quantity, threshold, status | `inventory-list-stock-status.spec.tsx` › shows available quantity, threshold and status for each item | unit | AC3 |
| 4. Filter by Low Stock, Out of Stock, or both | HTTP › should list both statuses with out of stock items first; should combine with other filters; should reject an unknown stock status. Dashboard › sends stock_status=… to the API as a list; does not send stock_status when the filter is not set | integration, unit | AC4; sort order from issue discussion (open question 2) |
| 5. Selecting an item opens its inventory detail page | Manual: click a row in the filtered list → the item's inventory detail page opens | manual | AC5 (existing row navigation, unchanged) |
| 6. Empty state when nothing matches | HTTP › should return an empty list when nothing matches. Module › returns nothing when no item has the status. Dashboard › shows the no results state when no items match the filter | integration, unit | AC6 |

Quantities and statuses reflect current data on load/refresh | HTTP › should combine with other filters (a reservation made before listing is reflected in the status); Manual: change an item's location quantity, reload the filtered list → the item's Available value, badge and filter membership update | integration, manual | AC7 |
| 8. Automated tests for filtering, statuses, empty state | All of the above, plus paging: HTTP › should paginate in quantity order and count all matches; Module › limits the first page to take | — | AC8 |
````

```markdown
## Requirements
- Tool required (manual mutation doesn't count): StrykerJS with the Jest runner for Medusa. Mutate only source files changed by the PR. Commit the config used; credit a teammate if reusing their setup (reusing your own #62 setup is fine).

- Submission: docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue>-njpiombino.md with template: title "# Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <title>"; header **PR(s):** **Tool:** **Config:** **Command:**; **Reports:** before/after links; **Mutation score:** before% -> after%; "## Surviving mutants" table | Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |; "## New or strengthened test" Commit · Test (file › name) · Kills; "## Questions" 1) what survivors revealed, 2) any survivor pointing to an assertion whose expected value wasn't from requirements, 3) AI use: what it produced and what was verified/corrected (or N/A). Q3 ends with a "Verified by me:" line the user supplies; the user must rerun Stryker themselves before submitting.
- The PR description's Test Evidence also links the D6 doc and gives the score (see [[pr-description-format]]).

## Working setup (from #62; reuse)
- Root dev deps already installed: `@stryker-mutator/core` and `@stryker-mutator/jest-runner` 10.1.1. `.gitignore` already ignores `.stryker-tmp` and `packages/modules/inventory/reports/mutation` (add the new package's reports dir).
- Config lives in the package dir: `packages/modules/inventory/stryker.config.json` + `stryker-build.cjs`. Copy both to the next package and change `mutate` (use a line range like `src/x.ts:443-553` to mutate only PR lines) and the file path in stryker-build.cjs. Run: `cd <package> && npx stryker run` with Postgres up (localhost:5433). About 7 min for 72 mutants and 48 tests.
- Key settings and why:
  - `testRunner: "jest"`, `jest.projectType: "custom"`, `configFile: "jest.config.js"`, a `testMatch` for the integration tests, `enableFindRelatedTests: false`.
  - Module integration tests load `dist/`, not `src/`, so `buildCommand` must rebuild after instrumentation. `buildCommand` is not run through a shell (`&&` breaks), so point it at a script.
  - `inPlace: true`: the sandbox copy breaks the package tsconfig's relative `extends`.
  - `coverageAnalysis: "all"`: `moduleIntegrationTestRunner` wraps suites in `describe("")`, so perTest coverage ids never match Jest test names and every mutant shows NoCoverage.
  - `concurrency: 1`: test runs share one DB name.
- Babel bug (both Stryker 10/Babel 8 and Stryker 9/Babel 7.29): instrumentation drops parameter decorators on params with a default value, so `@MedusaContext() context: Context = {}` loses its decorator and @EmitEvents tests fail in the initial run ("reading 'messageAggregator'"). `stryker-build.cjs` re-adds `@MedusaContext()` via regex before `yarn build`. Check that the target service uses the same `context: Context = {}` param name (some use `sharedContext`); adjust the regex if so.
- HTTP integration tests (`integration-tests/http`) can't be used: they boot a server against built packages. Mirror their cases as module-level tests so Stryker can see them.

## After each run
- Check `grep -c stryNS` in src and dist is 0. If dist is instrumented, rebuild the package (`yarn workspace <pkg> build`).
- Delete `src/migrations/.snapshot-*-integration-1.json`, which module test runs generate.
- Copy `reports/mutation/mutation.json` to the docs reports path; recompute scores from the JSON.
- A python snippet over `files[*].mutants` (status, location, replacement, and the source span) is the fastest way to list survivors with their original code.

## Typical #62 findings (for analysis)
Equivalent survivors were performance shortcuts (early returns on empty lists, narrowing a query to ids already filtered in memory, `select: ["id"]`). Real gaps were edge cases: first page with `take`, zero DB matches, caller's relations/select passed through, multiple invalid values in an error message. Removing equivalent shortcuts to raise the score was rejected (makes code worse).

**Why:** Graded deliverable that repeats for the next issue; setup took several failed runs to get right.
**How to apply:** Start from this recipe instead of rediscovering it; check the new package's test loader and decorator param names first.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-17 17:49:52Z)**_

I checked before changing anything, and the failure the reviewer describes doesn't happen.

**What I tested:** 70,000 matching items, more than Postgres's 65,535 limit on bound parameters per query. I ran all three risky paths: no other filters, combined with a SKU filter, and the full list with no page size. All three return correct results with no code change.

**Why it works:** I wrapped the Postgres client to record every query these paths send. MikroORM writes the ids directly into the SQL text (`id in ('iitem_bulk_1', ...)`) and sends **zero** bound parameters. So the 65,535 limit never comes into play. Postgres has no fixed cap on the length of the SQL text; the only cost is speed with very large lists. That cost is already noted in the code's `shortcut:` comment and in Tech Debt.

**Where things stand:** I added the three tests to the module spec as regression tests for the reviewer's scenario. They pass, take about 6.5 seconds, and aren't committed yet. The service code is unchanged.

Suggested reply to the reviewer:

> Good catch to check. I tested it with 70,000 matching items, which is past Postgres's 65,535 bound-parameter limit. MikroORM writes `IN` lists directly into the SQL, so no bound parameters are used and the limit doesn't apply. All three paths work, and I added them as regression tests in `inventory-module-service.spec.ts` (`stock_status filter with more ids than one query allows`). Very large lists only cost speed, which is already listed under Tech Debt.

**Decision for you:** the reviewer's other idea, skipping the intersection query when there are no other filters, is a few lines and saves one large query in that case. It's a speed improvement, not a fix, so I've left it out. If you want it anyway, I'll add it. It would change the mutation-tested lines, but the D6 doc points at commit `3c1a11d`, so it stays accurate.

Either way, the three new tests are ready to commit.

Stryker writes these after every run. They aren't new on each branch switch; they've been sitting on disk since your rerun.
